source.title: Dynamic Adversarial Fine-Tuning Reorganizes Refusal Geometry
source.authors: Wen-Hao Lan; Shan Li; Xin Lai; Mei-Qi Wu; Jun-Bin Yang; Hai-Hua Shen; Yi-Jun Yang

record.tranche_reason: The study forms harmful-minus-safe activation contrasts and causally ablates selected carriers, but finds that ablation at late R2D2 checkpoints strengthens refusal rather than removing it, and that the interventions cost benign utility. Its rank and subspace analyses also refine the low-dimensional account.
record.gate_note: The authors use harmful-minus-safe contrasts to rank candidate carriers; scores used only for carrier selection are not recorded as outcome rows. Rows below cover reported behavior, rank, carrier relocation, causal ablations, and utility effects. Cited findings from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study builds harmful-minus-safe difference-in-means carriers in Mistral-7B-v0.1 under SFT and R2D2 training. It ablates them during generation and reports HarmBench ASR, XSTest refusal and benign utility against no-intervention baselines. At late R2D2 checkpoints, ablation lowers ASR and raises safe-prompt refusal, the opposite of V1's prediction. SFT ablation does not remove refusal either. The same experiment bears on V4 (single direction vs top-3 subspace, effective rank) and V7 (carrier location and controllability differ by training regime).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that R2D2 relocates a low-dimensional, KL-admissible, utility-coupled refusal-control carrier along a robustness–utility frontier, with no dimensional expansion and with drift magnitude insufficient to explain robustness. They read late-stage ablation as restoring refusal (lower ASR, more over-refusal), not as removing it. They do not claim adaptive robustness or fail-closed redundancy.
record.recipe_differences: Uses harmful-minus-safe residual-stream contrasts and activation ablation, but selects a KL-admissible carrier from a pruned layer/position grid and tests selected-layer single and top-3 ablations at sparse checkpoints rather than ablating one direction at every layer and position. Does not test addition.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies by fine-tuning regime and checkpoint: R2D2 carrier location changes after step 100; early R2D2 checkpoints show maximal XSTest refusal and zero benign utility, while later checkpoints recover some utility and reopen attack success. Single-direction and top-3 intervention effects differ.

fits_no_version.finding: Regenerated adaptive attacks reopen late R2D2 checkpoints without the carrier being measured during the attacks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive GCG and AutoDAN ASR on R2D2 rises from 0 at step 50 to 0.613/0.270 at step 500.

fits_no_version.finding: R2D2 checkpoint trajectory: zero fixed-source ASR early, together with full XSTest over-refusal and zero benign utility; later checkpoints regain utility and reopen ASR. SFT stays at ASR ≈0.5–0.6.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dynamic adversarial fine-tuning trades over-refusal for robustness along a robustness–utility frontier.

record.code_released: The authors state a plan to release sanitized analysis code; URL not stated.
record.problems: One 7B backbone and two LoRA fine-tuning regimes; geometry comparisons use regime-native candidate libraries; only selected anchors receive causal interventions; the benign utility audit has 60 prompts and is not a broad capability benchmark; adaptive attacks cover only two attack families and three R2D2 checkpoints; no uncertainty estimates are reported for the listed outcomes.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted to meet the row limit. Dense trajectory summaries and geometry selection scores used only to select carriers are not separately recorded; the paper notes that the dense traces are monitors rather than its main mechanistic evidence.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal: addition is used only inside carrier-ranking scores, never as a behavioural test. Also untested: ablation at all layers and positions, Arditi-style direction selection (the last 20% of layers is excluded), and broad capability benchmarks.
No weight-edit or abliteration of released models.
Adaptive attacks are not analysed for carrier suppression. No training against ablation is tested.
No affine or cone representations tested. Only single vs top-3 ablation at one layer.
The authors explicitly do not separate harmfulness from refusal.
No transfer across languages, variants or base/instruct.
Only one backbone, one seed and two LoRA regimes. No pretraining-stage or other alignment-method comparison.

missing.what: SFT XSTest any-refusal under ablation: step 250 0.076→0.060 (single) / 0.080 (top-3); step 500 0.076→0.072 / 0.100. These show SFT ablation leaves safe-prompt refusal roughly unchanged.
Best admissible R2D2 carrier score falls from 1.91/1.94/1.84 (ref/50/100) to 1.13/1.07 (250/500); the refusal-side component drops from ~0.97 to ~0.20.
Largest top-3 principal angle at step 500: 42.55° for R2D2 vs 53.31° for SFT.
SFT benign utility under ablation, plotted only in Figure 7 with no numbers; the text says SFT shows no comparable utility collapse.
Causal tests at step 50 are said to run for both regimes, but only the R2D2 top-3 result is reported (no R2D2 single-direction, no SFT step 50).

record.verdict_notes: The reversed ablation effect may stem from the carrier-selection protocol rather than refute Arditi et al. outright. Selection uses a KL-admissibility filter and a COSMIC-style score, excludes the final 20% of layers, and picks layer 0, pos −3 at late R2D2 checkpoints. Ablation is applied at that one layer only. The verdicts therefore apply to this selected carrier in an adversarially trained LoRA model. Carrier-location rows r26–r31 are selection outcomes from a pruned grid; they are kept because they are the main geometry result. No uncertainty estimates are reported. Single 7B backbone and single seed.

versions.untested_parts: Tests ablation of a selected carrier at a selected layer and checkpoint, not projection at every layer and position. Does not test adding the direction. The 60-prompt benign audit is not a broad capability evaluation.
No weight-edit or released-model abliteration test.
Adaptive attacks are regenerated, but the study does not test whether they suppress the measured carrier or train against its ablation.

Measures local rank and compares single-direction with top-3 subspace ablations. Does not directly test affine or cone representations, or establish whether other refusal mechanisms exist beyond its candidate library.
The authors explicitly do not separate harmfulness representations from refusal-control representations.
No language, model-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer test.
Compares one backbone under SFT and R2D2 at selected checkpoints; does not establish general effects across model families, training methods, seeds, or a broader range of training schedules.

The authors say other layers and operators are not ruled out, so the result depends on layer and operator choice. Top-3 rows bear on V4, not V1.

relationships.reason: The training regime and step decide where the admissible carrier sits (late layer until R2D2 step 100, layer 0 after; SFT early by step 50) and how strongly ablation controls behaviour (large in late R2D2, weak in SFT) (r26–r43).

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Mistral-7B-v0.1, R2D2 vs SFT across checkpoints
